Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages).
Presently, students in the School of Professional Studies, URI’s School that primarily serves STAR (service-member, transfer, adult, and returning) students, need to decide between two bachelor’s of science degree programs: Nonprofit Administration and Professional Leadership Studies.
Although the programs’ courses are synergistic and students have an interest in exploring topics from both programs, these programs require students to take a strict set of courses.

Ultimately, there is little room for students to take courses in the other program from their major.
From a student perspective, this is limiting their opportunities for learning.
From a School perspective, this is increasing our difficulty to fill courses and best serve our students.
Our objective with this proposal is to provide greater flexibility for our students as a way to enhance their academic experience and establish more streamlined approaches for students to graduate.
By approving this proposal, the Professional Leadership Studies program would require students to take five courses as “major requirements” (15 credits).
Of these core courses, four of them would fulfill both majors.
One of them, SPC 420: Facilitating Leadership Development, would be the gateway course for the Professional Leadership Studies major designation.

2 In addition to those core courses, students would be required to take five courses as “major electives” (15 credits).
These could be selected from any of the SPC course offerings and based on availability and student interest.
Below is a written description of the changes.
Along with this proposal is a modified Curriculum Sheet to highlight these changes.

Proposals for all centers and institutes shall originate with faculty representing the disciplines concerned.
A proposal for the creation of a center or institute shall include an explanation of its goals and rationale, a description of its proposed administrative and staffing structure, a specific description of its relationship to other appropriate units of the University, a budget with personnel and space requirements, as well as amounts and sources of seed money.
A template for the application can be obtained from the Center Review subcommittee Subcommittee (CRS) of the Faculty Senate Research and Creative Activities Committee (RCAC).
Proposals are judged based on program quality, research, outreach, or educational activities, involvement of undergraduate and graduate students, interdepartmental or intercollege connections, and potential for continued financial viability, as appropriate for the mission and goals of the Center center or Institute institute.

Any specific arrangements for space, staff, financial support, or overhead return agreed to by the college, department or Vice President for Research and Economic Development should be documented in the application.
Applications approved by RCAC will be presented to the Faculty Senate for a vote prior to forwarding the application to the appropriate administrative office Vice President for Research and Economic Development and the Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs for final approval. #11-12–25, #17-18-23 #20-21-32 8.90.30 Review.
Centers and institutes shall be reviewed every four years by the Center Review Subcommittee (CRS) of the Committee for Research and Creative Activities (RCAC).
Additionally, continuing authorization to operate centers or institutes may be subject to review

by units and departments involved in the center or institute as well as review by the colleges of the involved departments.
A reporting template for the review can be obtained from the RCAC.
College reviews, if applicable, can be submitted as support documentation with this template.
Successful completion of the review will be based on overall program quality, research, outreach, or educational contributions, financial support, student involvement, interdepartmental or intercollege involvement, and continued external funding financial viability, as appropriate for the mission and goals of the center or institute.
The review of center’s and institute’s activities will be included in the RCAC’s report to the Faculty Senate annually.
Centers and institutes can be dissolved willingly by their leadership.
They can also be dissolved for failure to comply with the stated reporting process, or a failure to address and meet their stated goals.
The dissolution process will entail a CRS review, notice to the Faculty Senate, and a final determination by the Vice President for Research and Economic Development and the Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs.

Dissolved centers and institutes will be removed from the active centers lists.
Dissolved centers shall: remove webpages, materials, and signage from public view; and cease using the center's name for internal or external activities or funding.

1 FACULTY SENATE OFFICE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE March 24, 2022 Faculty Senate Curriculum and Standards Committee Report 2021-2022-7 At the March 3, 2022 meeting of the Curriculum and Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate.
SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate PROGRAM CHANGES: COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Business Analytics and Intelligence major: In 2007, the Management Information Systems major was suspended due to low enrollment and resource constraints.
The refreshed major will be renamed Business Analytics and Intelligence and will be offered, along with the previously approved minor, to help prepare students to meet the high demand for professionals.
As companies are increasingly data-driven, there is demand for business professionals with knowledge, skills, and abilities in business analytics and artificial intelligence.
As a result, there are many job opportunities and high average starting salaries associated with positions at a wide range of organizations.

There was a strategic gift from Al Verrecchia to help develop student competencies in the Artificial Intelligence space, and the university previously reallocated resources required to offer the major again.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Accounting major: The program change makes the number of credits required in the Accounting major 120 instead of 121.
A four-credit course that was required as part of the major is no longer required.
Therefore, it is possible to complete the degree requirements with 120 credits.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: General Business Administration major: General Business will go back to being a separate major and will no longer be a track in Management.
The program change that was made last year (where students would start coursework in fall 2023) resulted in confusion for students, faculty, and stakeholders.
The General Business major previously served over 200 majors each year, which makes it a critical offering for the College of Business and the University.

Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Management major: The proposed program change streamlines the options in the management major and distinguishes the management major from general business.
General Business will go back to being a separate major and will no longer be a track in Management.
The program change that was made last year (where students would start coursework in fall 2023) resulted in confusion for students, faculty, and stakeholders.
Bachelor of Science in Business Administration: Innovation and Entrepreneurship major: Update and revise requirements for major and minor as well as correct catalog copy.
